Subject: Dedicated sizing request — session-level sizing for Hypernova

Hi Marissa,

Thanks for taking this — were kicking off the pre-sales sizing work for Hypernova's conversational agents and want a session-level view rather than simple QPS. High level: multi-turn assistant (customer support + transactional ops), session stickiness matters (we route subsequent messages to the same session to preserve KV cache).

Rough numbers to start with:
- Concurrent active sessions (typical steady-state): ~1,200
- Concurrent sessions at peak (5–10 min window): ~4,200
- Average session duration: ~9 minutes
- Average turns per session: ~18 (mix of short prompts and long responses)
- Prompt tokens (avg): 120; response tokens (avg): 800
- Streaming responses: ~60% of calls (clients stream partial tokens back)
- Functions / tool-calls: ~8–12% of completions
- Session KV state: ~0.8–1.5 MB per session (dependencies: embeddings+small state)
- Target p95 latency for interactive calls: <= 250 ms (we understand p99 will be higher)
- SLA target: 99.9% uptime + regional redundancy for US east/west

We have a small sample of session logs that Ill attach (session_samples.csv) — it includes token counts per request/response and timestamps. Can you confirm the additional info you need to produce an initial GPU footprint (GPU class equivalents, warm pool sizing, and suggested burst capacity)? Also let me know if we should provide historical p99/p95 traces.

Procurement is ccd to get the ball rolling on NDA / T&Cs; wed like a ballpark before scheduling a workshop.

Cheers,
Alex Rivera
Head of Infrastructure, Hypernova AI

Thanks Alex — this is a great starting point, and the sample is very helpful. Quick acknowledgement: we can provide an initial sizing matrix and warm-pool recommendation based on session lifecycle assumptions, but Ill need a few clarifications to avoid over/underprovisioning. Can you answer the bullets below when you have a minute? If you prefer, we can capture this in the attached SLA-matrix-template.xlsx (Ill include it in this thread).

Key questions / clarifications (short):
- Percentiles for token lengths: p50/p90/p99 for both prompts and responses (sample-level numbers help us size KV cache & batching impact)
- Streaming behavior: when you say ~60% streaming, is that evenly spread or concentrated in a subset of endpoints?
- Function/tool-call distribution: are tools called early in the turn (affects latency) or at the end of a response (affects token output)?
- Session stickiness retention window: how long do sessions stay pinned before an idle timeout / eviction?
- KV size variability: is 0.8–1.5 MB typical per session or are there heavy tails (some sessions >10 MB)?
- Retry/fanout behaviors: do clients retry aggressively or fanout to multiple agents? Any long-polling websockets?
- Regional constraints: do you require strict US-east residency for traffic, or can we route to US-west for cold capacity?

Preliminary assumptions Im going to model if I dont hear back in 24 hours: p95 prompt length = 350 tokens, p95 response = 1800 tokens, 65% streaming, 10% tool-calls mid-response, sticky sessions evicted after 20 minutes idle, KV mean 1.1 MB with 95th at ~6 MB, retry rate ~1.03x, and we can assume regional routing preference to US-east with failover to US-west.

Next steps: once you confirm the bullets (or upload the completed SLA matrix), well run a quick synthetic runner to estimate GPU-hot-path utilization and return a recommended fleet footprint (A100/T4 equivalence, warm pool sizing, and autoscale thresholds). Ill also include a short list of SLO tradeoffs so procurement can see cost/latency options.

Would you like to schedule a 45-minute workshop this week with our solutions engineer (Karthik) and an infra architect? We can use that session to walk the sizing simulator and validate assumptions.

—
Marissa Cole

Alex — perfect, this is exactly the level of detail we need. I ran the completed SLA matrix through our sizing runner with the conservative tail assumptions you provided and here are preliminary outcomes and next steps (high level):

Preliminary sizing assumptions used (conservative):
- steady concurrent sessions: 1,200; peak concurrent sessions: 4,200
- p95 prompt: 350 tokens; p95 response: 1,800 tokens; p99 response heavy tail up to 5,200 tokens
- 65% streaming on chat endpoint; 12% function calls with 60% mid-response
- mean KV ~1.2 MB; 95th ~7 MB
- target interactive p95 <= 250 ms for non-tool calls; tool-invocation latency window expected to be higher

Preliminary recommendation (ballpark):
- Base reserved footprint: equivalent of 6 x A100-80GB GPUs (hot pool) to meet steady-state with aggressive batching + KV cache warm-pinning.
- Warm pool for bursts: ability to spin up an additional 3–5 GPUs within 60–120s for peak windows (autoscale policy + pre-warmed instances recommended).
- Long-tail handling: route ultra-long responses (>3k tokens) to an async tier (lower-cost instances) to avoid blocking hot-path GPUs; this mitigates p99 pressure and reduces cost.
- KV cache sizing: allocate cluster-level on-GPU KV caching for the top 75% of sessions and a spill-to-RAM policy for heavy tails; estimate ~1.2–1.5 GB of total KV RAM per 1,000 concurrent sessions (verify with telemetry).

Operational notes / tradeoffs to discuss in workshop:
- Lowering sticky timeout from 25m to 10m reduces steady warm-memory but increases miss rate and slightly raises p95 for session resume
- Increasing pre-warm lead time from 60s to 120s reduces cold-start CPU/GPU overhead at a modest cost
- Option: dedicated reserved capacity + short burst credits (helps predictability for procurement) vs. pure autoscale (lower cost but more variable latency)

Next steps I propose:
1) Schedule a 45-minute sizing workshop (Karthik + one infra architect) — can do Tue/Wed next week.
2) We'll run a small synthetic runner against your sample file and return an itemized GPU SKU & monthly cost estimate (12-month reserved vs. on-demand comparison).
3) If procurement wants an NDA or draft SOW before the workshop, send to sales_ops@redwood.ai and well accelerate.

If this preliminary footprint aligns with your expectations, Ill prepare a short slide with the cost ranges and a recommended cadence for follow-up (workshop + telemetry handoff).

Thanks — Ill book the workshop tentatively for Tue 09:00 PT and send a calendar invite; if thats bad, propose two windows and well adjust.
